_meta.description: Demo knowledge base of BIS hallmarking for BIS Sahayak AI prototype.
_meta.disclaimer: This is synthetic demo data created for hackathon prototyping. Hallmarking requirements, purity grades, and process details are illustrative. Authoritative hallmarking rules are published by BIS at https://www.bis.gov.in. Hallmarking was made compulsory in phases — verify the current list of mandatory districts.

hallmarking.title: Gold Hallmarking — Purity Grades
hallmarking.description: BIS hallmarking of gold jewellery certifies the purity of gold content. Gold purity is measured in carats (K) or fineness. BIS recognises three standard purity grades for gold jewellery.
hallmarking.process_summary: Jewellery submitted to BIS-recognised Assaying and Hallmarking Centre. Purity verified by XRF or fire assay. If compliant, three marks are affixed: BIS logo, purity grade (fineness number), and hallmarking centre's identification mark along with year of hallmarking.
hallmarking.verification_method: Consumers can verify hallmark authenticity using the BIS Care mobile application by entering the hallmark number.

hallmarking.title: Silver Hallmarking — Purity Grades
hallmarking.description: BIS hallmarking of silver articles certifies the purity of silver content. Silver purity is expressed as fineness (parts per thousand).
hallmarking.process_summary: Silver articles submitted to BIS-recognised Assaying and Hallmarking Centre. Purity tested and hallmark affixed if compliant. Includes BIS logo, fineness number, and centre identification mark.
hallmarking.verification_method: Verify via BIS Care app or by contacting the hallmarking centre directly.

hallmarking.title: Assaying and Hallmarking Centre Recognition
hallmarking.description: BIS recognises assaying and hallmarking centres (AHCs) that meet specified competence criteria. These centres are authorised to test and hallmark gold and silver articles under the BIS hallmarking scheme.
recognition_requirements: XRF or fire assay equipment capability
Quality management system per BIS requirements
Traceability of measurements to national standards
centre_obligations: Maintain accuracy and traceability of assaying results
Keep records of all articles assayed and hallmarked
Report hallmarking data to BIS periodically

hallmarking.title: Compulsory Hallmarking — District Coverage
hallmarking.description: The Government of India has progressively expanded compulsory hallmarking of gold jewellery and artefacts. The list of districts where hallmarking is mandatory has been expanded in phases.
key_points: Compulsory hallmarking was first notified in 2021 for 256 districts
Both jewellers and customers are expected to ensure hallmarked gold jewellery
Exemptions apply for certain categories (e.g., articles weighing below specified limits, exports)
exemptions: Jewellery weighing below minimum threshold (verify current BIS notification)
Special occasion or religious jewellery as notified

hallmarking.title: BIS Hallmarking Marks — Identification Guide
hallmarking.description: A BIS-hallmarked article carries three distinct marks. Understanding these marks helps consumers verify the authenticity and purity of their gold or silver jewellery.

marks_on_article.description: The Bureau of Indian Standards logo (triangle shape with 'BIS' text) indicating the article has been hallmarked at a BIS-recognised centre.
A three-digit number (e.g., 916, 750, 585 for gold; 925, 900 for silver) indicating the purity of the precious metal.
A unique mark or code identifying the BIS-recognised Assaying and Hallmarking Centre that tested and hallmarked the article, along with the year of hallmarking.
